title: Java News Roundup: TornadoVM 7.0, Groovy 6.0, GraalVM, Hibernate, Quarkus, Gradle, Maven
gist: Weekly Java roundup: GA of TornadoVM 7.0 and Groovy 6.0, JEP 544 AOT code compilation proposed to target JDK 28, Maven 4.0 RC7 as likely last before GA, Gradle 9.8.0, and Quarkus 3.39.5 fixing 32 CVEs, which the Quarkus team attributes to AI discovering many CVEs.

insights.claim: Quarkus 3.39.5 resolves 32 CVEs across its ecosystem, and the Quarkus team attributes the volume to AI discovering many CVEs these days.
insights.speaker: Quarkus team
insights.so_what: AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery raises patching workload across open-source stacks.
insights.quote: AI discovers a lot of CVEs these days, and Quarkus aggregates a lot of components.

insights.claim: JEP 544, Ahead-of-Time Code Compilation, was proposed to target JDK 28 to make optimized native code available at HotSpot start for faster startup, warmup and peak performance.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Improves Java competitiveness for cloud/serverless where startup time matters.

insights.claim: JEP 546 (adaptive heap sizing for ZGC) and JEP 545 (faster startup and warmup with ZGC) advanced to Candidate status.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Better resource efficiency for Java in shared/containerized environments.
insights.locator: JEP 546, Adaptive Heap Sizing for ZGC

insights.claim: Gradle 9.8.0 adds Java 27 support and a claimed 45% performance improvement on Windows.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich

insights.claim: Apache Maven 4.0 RC7 is expected to be the last release candidate before GA in the coming weeks pending community feedback.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Major Java build tool version transition imminent.
insights.quote: the coming weeks pending community feedback.
insights.locator: The seventh release candidate of Apache Maven

insights.claim: TornadoVM 7.0 adds a TileContext class complementing KernelContext and @Parallel for writing GPU kernels in Java.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Java expanding into GPU compute workloads.

insights.claim: Jakarta EE 12 Core Profile is planned for release before JakartaOne Livestream on December 1st, and a new Jakarta CRaC specification is open for review.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Enterprise Java spec cadence; CRaC targets startup performance.
insights.locator: In his weekly Hashtag Jakarta EE blog

insights.claim: Spring teams shipped second milestones of Spring Boot, Framework, Security and others, and first milestones of Spring AI and Spring Cloud.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Spring AI inclusion signals mainstream Java frameworks integrating AI.
insights.locator: It was a busy week over at Spring

insights.claim: Micrometer Tracing 1.8.0 deprecates Zipkin Exporter support because OpenTelemetry discontinued it in version 1.65.0.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.locator: The second milestone release of Micrometer Tracing

insights.claim: Open Liberty 26.0.0.10 beta supports JDK 27, noting G1 is now the default GC in all environments, which may change GC behavior in constrained environments.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Operational change for constrained Java deployments.
insights.locator: The beta release of Open Liberty
